about: Swole Doge vs. Cheems puts two Shiba Inus side by side on a white background. On the left is Doge with his head photoshopped onto an absurdly muscular bodybuilder torso, standing tall and calm. On the right is Cheems, the chubby, slouching Shiba, sitting with blue tears running down his face. The joke is a mock-heroic comparison: the left side is a glorified, usually older version of something (ancient warriors, old-school games, your grandparents) and the right side is the soft modern equivalent that falls apart over the smallest inconvenience. The exaggeration on both sides is the point, so it reads as affectionate nostalgia rather than a serious argument.
origin: The pairing grew out of two existing dog memes: the long-running Doge photo and Cheems, a Shiba known for slurred, extra-m spellings like "cheemsburger". Spanish-language Facebook meme pages started putting a buff Doge next to a crying Cheems in early 2020, and the format spread to Reddit and English-speaking pages that spring.
usage:
There are two boxes across the top. The left box labels Swole Doge, the strong, idealized "then" version. The right box labels Cheems, the weak "now" version. The classic setup is the same thing in two eras, like "phones in 2005" and "phones in 2026", but you can also compare two groups, two versions of yourself or two products.

It works best when the left side is boastful and the right side is pathetically specific. A short caption under each label helps, for example "could survive being dropped off a building" vs "cracks if you look at it". Keep the labels parallel so the contrast reads instantly.
ideas: phones in 2005: survived a fall down the stairs
phones now: cracked screen from a pocket
me at 8 years old: played outside till dark
me at 30: tired after one email
games in 2004: whole game on the disc
students before google: library card catalog
goalkeepers in the 90s: no gloves needed
goalkeepers now: injured by a light breeze
